summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: The identification of DNA as genetic material proceeded through 3 milestones: (1) Griffith (1928): Heat-killed smooth S-strain transformed rough R-strain into virulent S-strain; (2) Avery, MacLeod, McCarty (1944): DNase enzyme alone abolished transformation; (3) Hershey & Chase (1952): T2 bacteriophage ^32P-DNA entered bacterial pellet while ^35S-protein remained in supernatant, providing unequivocal proof.

conceptBreakdown.content:
### 1.1 Griffith’s Bacterial Transformation Experiment (1928)
- Working with *Streptococcus pneumoniae* (Pneumococcus), Frederick Griffith identified two strains:
  - **S-Strain (Smooth)**: Virulent; possesses a smooth mucopolysaccharide (glycocalyx) capsule; causes fatal pneumonia in mice.
  - **R-Strain (Rough)**: Avirulent; lacks a capsule; non-pathogenic.

```
                        GRIFFITH'S EXPERIMENTAL PROTOCOL
                        
   1. Live S-Strain ─────────────► Inject into Mice ──► Mice DIE (Live S recovered)
   2. Live R-Strain ─────────────► Inject into Mice ──► Mice SURVIVE
   3. Heat-Killed S-Strain ──────► Inject into Mice ──► Mice SURVIVE
   4. Heat-Killed S + Live R ───► Inject into Mice ──► Mice DIE (Live S recovered!)
```

- **Conclusion**: Heat-killed S-strain bacteria transferred a heat-stable **"Transforming Principle"** to live R-strain cells, transforming them into virulent S-strain cells.

### 1.2 Avery, MacLeod, & McCarty’s Biochemical Characterization (1944)
- Purified biochemical fractions from heat-killed S-cells:
  - Treatment with **Proteases** $\longrightarrow$ Transformation OCCURRED.
  - Treatment with **RNase** $\longrightarrow$ Transformation OCCURRED.
  - Treatment with **DNase** $\longrightarrow$ Transformation **INHIBITED**.
- **Conclusion**: DNA is the transforming principle and the chemical basis of heredity.

### 1.3 Hershey & Chase Bacteriophage Experiment (1952)
- Used $T_2$ bacteriophages infecting *Escherichia coli*:
  - Batch 1: $^{35}\text{S}$ labeled viral protein coat $\longrightarrow$ Radioactivity found in **SUPERATANT** (phage ghosts).
  - Batch 2: $^{32}\text{P}$ labeled viral DNA core $\longrightarrow$ Radioactivity found in **BACTERIAL PELLET**.
- **Conclusion**: DNA is the genetic material injected by phages into host cells.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Differential Isotope Labeling Logic
conceptBreakdown.title: Differential Isotope Labeling Logic
conceptBreakdown.content: Proteins contain Sulfur (in Methionine/Cysteine) but no Phosphorus, so ^35S selectively labels viral coats; Nucleic acids contain Phosphorus (in phosphodiester backbones) but no Sulfur, so ^32P selectively labels the DNA core.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Pneumococcal Capsule Virulence Factor
conceptBreakdown.title: Pneumococcal Capsule Virulence Factor
conceptBreakdown.content: The smooth polysaccharide capsule of S-strain prevents phagocytosis by host alveolar macrophages, conferring full lethality in mammalian hosts.
